newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts shrug off strong auction, eyes on FOMC.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts shrug off strong auction, eyes on FOMC.

text.p: UK gilts shed their early gains despite a strong auction of five-year notes as the market braced itself for the outcome of a Federal Open Market Committee meeting to discuss U.S. interest rates.

Earlier the market rose on optimism before the auction which saw the Bank of England sell 1.5 billion stg of 7.0 percent gilts due 2002, garnering cover of 3.03 times. But by early afternoon June gilts were up just 2/32 at 113-16/32 after market optimism before the auction carried them briefly up to 113-21/32. "It was a very good result but the market hasn't really responded. It may well need to come back to around 113-12 before we can go on," one saleswoman at a market-maker said.

"It may well be that the FOMC is putting a bit of a cap on the market," she said. A narrow majority of top U.S. bond dealers surveyed by Reuters -- 21 out of 39 -- said they expect the central bank to hold rates steady, at least for now.

Dealers said they thought the UK bonds offered for auction had gone into fairly safe hands although there was some concern about a rumour that a market-maker was sitting on a sizeable chunk of the stock.
"It perhaps hasn't gone into hands that are as safe as we'd like," a salesman at a UK brokerage said.
He added that he thought much of the demand for the bonds came from operators who were switching out of other gilts rather than from an influx of new money.
